issue_context.title: Spotify Integration - media_position_updated_at not updated when media_position is
issue_context.body:
### The problem

`media_position_updated_at` is not updated when `media_position` is updated (with the exception of initial play/pause). Additionally, `media_position` is updated more frequently than on initial play and pause. It looks like the position is being updated every 30 seconds. This seems different than other media_player entities where `media_position` is only updated on initial play and pause, and `media_player_updated_at` is always updated when `media_position` is.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.1.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Spotify

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/spotify/

### Diagnostics information

Not Available

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing in the logs but here are a couple of template outputs

```


### Additional information

https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/issues/101

Not stale. This is still an issue with 2023.8.4

After diving into the code, I've noticed that this integration uses Spotify's API data to determine the `media_position_updated_at` property. More specifically, the [timestamp property of the currently playing track endpoint](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/reference/get-the-users-currently-playing-track).

Sadly, the description is not accurate. It suggests that it returns the timestamp of when the data was fetched. But in my investigation, this value updates randomly. [And I'm not the only one who noticed that.](https://community.spotify.com/t5/Spotify-for-Developers/API-playback-timestamp/td-p/5291948)

I've worked out a bugfix and will create a PR later today.

review_comments: Can you maybe react with a link to this in a comment? I'm curious about this

There is a discussion in this archived repo: https://github.com/spotify/web-api/issues/1073 
You can also test it yourself here: https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/reference/get-the-users-currently-playing-track

On that page start a song, click the "try it" button, and observe `timestamp`. Click the "try it" button again and the other data will be updated (such as `progress_ms`), but `timestamp` will remain the same. Which does not follow their description `Unix Millisecond Timestamp when data was fetched.`
Oh I didn't even know you could execute that easy on their page. Understood! Thanks!
